newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to step up "Buy Russian" campaign.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to step up "Buy Russian" campaign.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin plans to shift a "Buy Russian" campaign up a gear by asking millions of Russians to do their bit to help ailing national industries, the Kremlin said on Monday.

Yeltsin's spokesman told Itar-Tass news agency that the president, who has ordered officials to change their posh foreign cars for less glamourous Russian models, would focus on his new campaign in a radio address on Tuesday.
"He plans to develop his call to Russians to show a preference for home-made products," Tass said, quoting presidential press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky.
"Buy Russian goods, they are our goods," Yeltsin said last week, announcing his campaign, but made clear it would not mean restrictions on imports.

Some reports say up to half of the food consumed by Russians is imported. Russians prefer in many cases to buy Western products, particularly electronic goods, because the equivalent items manufactured in Russia do not meet world standards.
The 66-year-old Kremlin leader is trying to counter public discontent about the state of affairs in Russia.

He reshuffled his cabinet last month to reinforce it with young reformers, launched a crusade against corruption and vowed to take measures which, after decades of fruitless efforts, would make bribe-taking a risky business.

Yeltsin has criticised one official after another in recent weeks, partly to show he is back at the helm after months of illness and to show he is tackling Russia's problems. He broke from that practice on Monday by offering some praise.

He told Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin the government had worked better since the reshuffle, Tass said. Yeltsin told Chernomyrdin he appreciated his efforts and described the 59-year-old premier as an "experienced person".
Some of Chernomyrdin's responsibilities for overseeing the economy have gone to two young first deputies -- Boris Nemtsov, 37, and Anatoly Chubais, 41.
Chubais and Nemtsov have vowed to take radical measures to end chronic non-payments in industry and delays in wages and pensions which are strangling the economy.

Yeltsin also commended the recent work of Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, an opponent of NATO expansion and an advocate of closer ties with neighbouring Belarus, despite the West's criticism of authoritarian President Alexander Lukashenko.
He praised Primakov's mediation at talks between the former Soviet republic of Moldova and its breakaway Dnestr region which brought a breakthrough last week towards a normalisation of their ties.
"Frankly speaking I was proud of you," Tass quoted Yeltsin as telling Primakov.
Yeltsin's praise represented a vote of support for Primakov, who had been accused by Russian media of pushing too hard for a union deal with Belarus.

Primakov, who has been seeking ways to counterbalance NATO's planned expansion eastwards, had pushed a draft of a union treaty which was later watered down because critics saw it as harmful for Russia's economy and its fledgling democracy.
Priamkov faces a new round of talks with NATO Secretary General Javier Solana on Tuesday on an agreement to map out Moscow's relations with the Western defence alliance.
